extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies preparing NEPA documents, cooperating agencies, applicants, and public commenters / NEPA practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for preparing, publishing, commenting on, responding to, and implementing Environmental Impact Statements (EIS) under NEPA, including scoping, alternatives, analysis of environmental consequences, consultation, dispute resolution, records of decision, and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and need statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief summary that summarizes the underlying purpose and need for the proposed agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be concise and provide the basis for identifying and evaluating alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives section – centrality and comparative form
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives section is the heart of the EIS and should identify the reasonably foreseeable environmental effects of the proposed action and the alternatives in comparative form based on affected environment and environmental consequences analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis should sharply define issues for decision makers and the public and provide a clear basis for choice among options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous exploration and objective evaluation of reasonable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall rigorously explore and objectively evaluate reasonable alternatives to the proposed action, and briefly discuss reasons for eliminating alternatives from detailed study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency need not consider every conceivable alternative but must consider a reasonable range that fosters informed decision making; may include reasonable alternatives outside the lead agency's jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss each alternative in detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss each alternative considered in detail, including the proposed action, so reviewers may evaluate comparative merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis should enable reviewers to compare alternatives based on presented data and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the no action alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS must include the no action alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The no action alternative should serve as the baseline against which the proposed action and other alternatives are compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify preferred alternative(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the agency's preferred alternative or alternatives in the draft statement and identify such alternative in the final statement unless another law prohibits expression of such preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps the public and decisionmakers understand agency inclination and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appropriate mitigation measures in alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate mitigation measures not already included in the proposed action or alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation should be described in sufficient detail to inform analyses and decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify environmentally preferable alternative(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the environmentally preferable alternative(s) among the alternatives considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmentally preferable alternative best promotes NEPA's national environmental policy by maximizing environmental benefits (e.g., addressing climate change effects, protecting historic/tribal/natural resources, or causing least damage). The environmentally preferable alternative may be proposed action, no action, or another reasonable alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affected environment – concise description
rubrics_metrics.description: Succinctly describe the environment of the area(s) to be affected by the alternatives, including reasonably foreseeable environmental trends and planned actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description should be no longer than necessary to understand the relevant affected environment and the effects of alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of high-quality information in describing affected environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall use high-quality information, including reliable data, models, and Indigenous Knowledge, to describe reasonably foreseeable environmental trends including anticipated climate-related changes, and when such information is incomplete provide information consistent with §1502.21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data and analyses should be commensurate with importance of the effect; less important material summarized, consolidated, or referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid useless bulk; focus on important issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of the affected environment should concentrate effort and attention on important issues; verbose descriptions are not a measure of adequacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid including needless volume; tailor level of detail to significance of effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental consequences – analytic basis for comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: The environmental consequences section forms the scientific and analytic basis for the comparisons of alternatives and shall consolidate required NEPA discussions within EIS scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparison should be based on reasonably foreseeable effects and significance, focusing on significant or important effects; should not duplicate alternatives section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze adverse environmental effects that cannot be avoided
rubrics_metrics.description: Include analysis of any adverse environmental effects that cannot be avoided should the proposal be implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify unavoidable harms associated with implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze effects of the no action alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Include analysis of the effects of the no action alternative, including any adverse environmental effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No action provides the baseline for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term uses vs long-term productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the relationship between short-term uses of the human environment and the maintenance and enhancement of long-term productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss tradeoffs between immediate benefits and long-term environmental productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreversible or irretrievable commitments of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze any irreversible or irretrievable commitments of Federal resources that would be involved if the proposal is implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify resource losses that cannot be reversed or recovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts with plans, policies, controls (including climate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, analyze possible conflicts between the proposed action and objectives of Federal, regional, State, Tribal, and local plans, policies, and controls for the area concerned, including those addressing climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify inconsistencies and discuss relevance to decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate change-related effects analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, include climate change-related effects, including, where feasible, quantification of greenhouse gas emissions, from the proposed action and alternatives and the effects of climate change on the proposed action and alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate climate impacts both as caused by and affecting the proposal; quantify GHGs when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy requirements and conservation potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, analyze energy requirements and conservation potential of various alternatives and mitigation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessments of energy use and potential for conservation improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural or depletable resource requirements and conservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, analyze natural or depletable resource requirements and conservation potential of various alternatives and mitigation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess resource demands and opportunities to conserve limited resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk reduction, resiliency, and adaptation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, analyze relevant risk reduction, resiliency, or adaptation measures incorporated into the proposed action or alternatives, informed by relevant science and data on the affected environment and expected future conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how alternatives incorporate measures to reduce risk and increase resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urban quality, historic/cultural resources, and built environment design
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, analyze urban quality, historic and cultural resources, and the design of the built environment, including reuse and conservation potential of alternatives and mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include design and cultural resource considerations in comparative analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation measures to mitigate adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Include means to mitigate adverse environmental effects (if not fully covered under alternatives section mitigation requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe mitigation measures and their expected effectiveness; cross-reference alternatives section as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic and technical considerations including economic benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, analyze economic and technical considerations, including the economic benefits of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When economic/social effects interrelate with natural/physical environmental effects, discuss them; economic/social effects alone do not require an EIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disproportionate and adverse effects on communities with environmental justice concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, analyze disproportionate and adverse human health and environmental effects on communities with environmental justice concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and analyze effects that fall disproportionately on vulnerable communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of economic and social effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic or social effects by themselves do not require preparation of an EIS, but when interrelated with natural/physical environmental effects, the EIS shall discuss these effects on the human environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain linkages and interactions between social/economic and environmental effects where they are related.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of scoping information in draft EIS or appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft EIS or appendix shall include a summary of information, including alternatives and analyses, submitted by commenters during scoping for agency consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document what scoping input informed the development of the draft EIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Append scoping comments to draft EIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency shall append to the draft EIS or publish all comments (or summaries where exceptionally voluminous) received during the scoping process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure scoping record is available to reviewers and decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of preparers and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: EIS shall list names and qualifications (expertise, experience, professional disciplines) of persons primarily responsible for preparing the EIS or important background papers, and identify persons responsible for particular analyses where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List normally will not exceed two pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appendix is prepared, it shall be published with the EIS and consist of material prepared in connection with the EIS; material substantiating any analysis fundamental to the EIS; material relevant to the decision; scoping comments for draft EIS; and for final EIS, comment summaries and responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix should include documents and substantiating analyses that are necessary for understanding key EIS conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and distribution of EIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall publish the entire draft and final EIS and unchanged statements and transmit the entire statement electronically (or paper if requested) to Federal agencies with jurisdiction or expertise, appropriate Federal/State/Tribal/local agencies, the applicant, any requester, and in final EIS any person/organization that submitted substantive comments on the draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure broad and accessible distribution of the full EIS to interested parties and authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make incomplete or unavailable information explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating reasonably foreseeable significant effects and information is incomplete or unavailable, the agency shall make clear that such information is lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about data gaps is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include essential information if costs reasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: If incomplete information relevant to reasonably foreseeable significant effects is essential to a reasoned choice among alternatives, and overall costs of obtaining it are not unreasonable, the agency shall include the information in the EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and present crucial data unless cost/feasibility is unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: If information cannot be obtained include statements and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: If information cannot be obtained because costs are unreasonable or means unknown, the EIS shall include: (1) a statement that such information is incomplete or unavailable; (2) a statement of relevance of the missing information; (3) a summary of existing credible scientific evidence relevant to effects evaluation; and (4) the agency's evaluation of such effects based on theoretical approaches or accepted research methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a reasoned, evidence-based evaluation even when key data are unavailable; identify the limits of the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably foreseeable includes low-probability catastrophic effects when supported
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this section, 'reasonably foreseeable' includes effects that have catastrophic consequences even if their probability is low, provided analysis is supported by credible scientific evidence, not pure conjecture, and within the rule of reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore low-probability high-consequence risks if credible evidence supports analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-benefit analysis incorporation and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If considering a cost-benefit analysis relevant to choices among alternatives with different environmental effects, the agency shall incorporate it by reference or append it, and discuss its relationship to analyses of unquantified environmental impacts and values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies need not display weighing of merits/drawbacks in monetary terms for NEPA compliance and should avoid monetization when important qualitative considerations exist; indicate considerations including non-environmental factors relevant to the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate EIS preparation with other federal environmental reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: To the fullest extent possible, agencies shall prepare draft EISs concurrent and integrated with environmental impact analyses and related surveys/studies required by other Federal environmental laws and Executive Orders (e.g., Fish and Wildlife Coordination Act, NHPA, ESA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate to avoid duplication and to meet overlapping legal requirements in an integrated manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: List required Federal permits, licenses, and authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft EIS shall list all Federal permits, licenses, and other authorizations that must be obtained in implementing the proposal; if uncertain whether a Federal authorization is necessary, the draft EIS shall so indicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify regulatory triggers and uncertainties to inform review and permitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite and request comments from appropriate agencies and public
rubrics_metrics.description: After preparing a draft EIS and before preparing a final EIS, the agency shall obtain comments from Federal agencies with jurisdiction/expertise and request comments of appropriate State, Tribal, and local agencies, governments that may be affected, any agency that requested it, the applicant, and the public, affirmatively soliciting comments to inform interested persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may also request comments on a final EIS before the final decision and should provide for electronic submission with reasonable accessibility measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to comment for cooperating and standards agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperating agencies and agencies authorized to develop and enforce environmental standards shall comment within the time period specified; a Federal agency may reply it has no comment if satisfied the EIS reflects its views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely participation by agencies with jurisdiction/expertise is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of public and agency comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments shall be as specific as possible and may address adequacy of the statement or merits of alternatives; comments should explain why issues raised are important, reference corresponding section/page numbers, propose specific changes, and describe data/sources/methodologies supporting proposed changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific, substantiated comments better inform agency responses and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When criticizing predictive methodology propose alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: When a participating agency criticizes a lead agency's predictive methodology, it should describe the alternative methodology it prefers and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive methodological alternatives with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating agency specification of additional information needed
rubrics_metrics.description: A cooperating agency shall specify whether it needs additional information to fulfill other environmental review or consultation requirements and identify what information it needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about information gaps that prevent fulfillment of consultation or permitting duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating agency specification of necessary mitigation and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A cooperating agency with jurisdiction by law shall specify mitigation measures it considers necessary to allow it to grant or approve applicable authorizations or concurrences and cite its applicable statutory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie mitigation requests to legal authority to facilitate resolution and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of substantive comments and possible responses
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency preparing a final EIS shall consider substantive comments timely submitted and shall respond to individual comments or groups of comments; in the final EIS, the agency may respond by modifying alternatives, developing/evaluating new alternatives, supplementing/modifying analyses, making factual corrections, or explaining why comments do not warrant further response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are not required to respond to each comment but must address substantive issues; responses should be evidenced and reasoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish or append all substantive comments and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall append or otherwise publish all substantive comments received on the draft EIS (or summaries where exceptionally voluminous) and responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the public record of comments and agency responses available with the final EIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of errata sheets for minor changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If changes in response to comments are minor and confined to factual corrections or explaining why comments do not warrant further response, an agency may write changes on errata sheets and attach them to the statement instead of rewriting the draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, publish the final statement including the errata sheet, a copy of the draft statement, the comments, and the responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of dispute resolution and pre-decisional referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish procedures for referring Federal interagency disagreements concerning proposed major Federal actions that might cause unsatisfactory environmental effects, provide means for early resolution, and encourage agencies to engage early to resolve disagreements before referring disputes to the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also establishes procedures to request informal dispute resolution by the Council on NEPA issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early interagency coordination and dispute resolution processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should engage in interagency coordination and collaboration early in planning and decision-making, identify and resolve disputes as early as practicable, and elevate issues timely to appropriate officials or the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may request Council informal dispute resolution by providing a summary of the proposed action, disputed issues, and contacts; the Council may offer non-binding recommendations or convene meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to weigh for Council referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding what environmental objections are appropriate to refer to the Council, an agency should weigh potential adverse environmental effects considering possible violation of national standards/policies, severity, geographical scope, duration, importance as precedents, availability of environmentally preferable alternatives, economic and technical considerations (including costs of delay), and other appropriate considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh these factors to determine whether to refer an issue to the Council after timely attempts to resolve differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral notification, content, and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The referring agency shall notify the lead agency as early as possible, include notification in comments when practicable, identify essential information lacking, deliver referral to the Council no later than 25 days after the lead agency made the final EIS available (or after EA is made available), and the referral shall consist of a signed letter to the lead agency and a statement supported by factual evidence detailing disputed facts, violated requirements/policies, reasons for referral, national importance finding, steps taken to raise concerns, and recommendations for mitigation/alternatives/further study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict timelines apply; except when the lead agency grants an extension, the Council will not accept referrals after 25 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead agency response to referral
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 25 days after referral, the lead agency may deliver a response to the Council and referring agency addressing issues raised, supported by evidence/explanations, and giving the lead agency's response to recommendations. The lead agency may request more time if it assures the matter will not go forward in the interim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response must be substantive and evidence-based; applicants and interested persons may file views in writing no later than the response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council actions and timelines on referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 25 days after receipt of referral and any response (or upon being informed there will be no response), the Council may conclude resolution, initiate mediation discussions, obtain additional views (including public meetings), determine issue not of national importance, request further negotiation, publish findings and recommendations, or when appropriate submit referral and response with the Council's recommendation to the President. The Council shall take no longer than 60 days to complete specified actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council's review is time-limited and may include public involvement; referral process is not intended to create private rights or be judicially reviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of decision content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of decision, each agency shall prepare and timely publish a concise public record of decision that states the decision; identifies alternatives considered and the environmentally preferable alternative(s); specifies factors (environmental, economic, technical, statutory missions) balanced in making the decision and how they entered into it; and states whether the agency adopted all practicable means to mitigate environmental harm and if not why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ROD should identify authority for enforceable mitigation and prepare a monitoring and compliance plan consistent with §1505.3(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementing the decision – mitigation and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may provide monitoring to assure decisions are carried out, and mitigation and other conditions established in the EIS or during its review and committed as part of the decision shall be implemented by the lead or other consenting agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mitigation conditions in grants, permits, or approvals and condition funding on mitigation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider environmental justice in mitigation and decision implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead or cooperating agency should, where relevant, incorporate mitigation measures that address significant human health and environmental effects that disproportionately and adversely affect communities with environmental justice concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly tailor mitigation to ameliorate disproportionate impacts where identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and compliance plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When analysis of reasonably foreseeable effects is based on implementation of mitigation and the agency incorporates mitigation into a ROD, FONSI, or separate decision document, the agency shall prepare and publish a monitoring and compliance plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan should be tailored to mitigation complexity and include: (1) description of mitigation measures; (2) parties responsible; (3) how monitoring info will be publicly available if appropriate; (4) anticipated timeframe; (5) standards for determining compliance and consequences of non-compliance; and (6) how mitigation will be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring does not itself trigger supplementation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an action is incomplete or ongoing, an agency does not need to supplement its EIS or EA or revise its ROD or FONSI solely based on new information developed through a monitoring and compliance plan required by this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing implementation of a monitoring plan is not considered an incomplete or ongoing Federal action for purposes of supplementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on agency actions during NEPA process
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided by exceptions, until an agency issues a FONSI or ROD, no action concerning the proposal may be taken that would have an adverse environmental effect or limit the choice of reasonable alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve decision space during environmental review to avoid prejudicing the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for applicant planning and preparatory activities
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency considering an application may authorize applicant activities (planning, designs, acquisition of land interests, purchase of long lead-time equipment, etc.) necessary to support an application if the agency determines such activities would not limit choice of reasonable alternatives and notifies the applicant that the agency retains discretion to select any reasonable alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits preparatory actions that do not prejudice NEPA choices but requires agency notification and discretion retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on interim major Federal actions during program-level review
rubrics_metrics.description: While work on a required environmental review for a program is in progress and action is not covered by an existing environmental document, agencies shall not undertake in the interim any major Federal action covered by the program that may significantly affect the human environment unless the action is justified independently, accompanied by an adequate environmental review, and will not prejudice the ultimate decision on the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim actions that tend to determine subsequent development or limit alternatives prejudice the ultimate decision and are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation to eliminate duplication with State, Tribal, and local procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: To the fullest extent practicable unless prohibited by law, agencies shall cooperate with State, Tribal, and local agencies to reduce duplication between NEPA and comparable State, Tribal, and local requirements through joint planning, research, hearings, environmental assessments, and joint EISs where practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One document may be used to comply with multiple laws where requirements are not in conflict; joint lead agencies may be designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss inconsistencies with State, Tribal, local plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental impact statements shall discuss any inconsistency of a proposed action with any approved State, Tribal, or local plan or law and describe the extent to which the agency would reconcile its proposed action with the plan or law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA requires discussion of inconsistencies but does not require reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of another agency's EIS or EA with independent review
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt another agency's draft or final EIS or EA, or portion thereof, provided the adopting agency conducts an independent review and concludes that it meets standards for an adequate statement or assessment and follows requirements for republication or supplementation as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If actions covered are substantially the same, republish and file as final; if not, treat as draft or supplement and republish. Cooperating agencies may issue ROD adopting the lead agency's EIS without republication in some cases.
